summary: At 75 people per square mile spread across nearly 82 square miles, Durham is less a town than a landscape with a town stitched into it — a patchwork of almond and walnut orchards, rice fields, and open rangeland on the Sacramento Valley floor about ten miles south of Chico. That flat, wide-open agricultural setting delivers unobstructed views of the Sierra Nevada foothills to the east and the Sutter Buttes — often called the world's smallest mountain range — rising from the valley floor to the south. The median home value of $612,100 against a median household income of roughly $121,000 puts the price-to-income ratio around 5:1, which is stiff but notably less punishing than coastal California; median rent at $1,092 is remarkably low by state standards, reflecting the rural reality that most housing here is owner-occupied on larger lots rather than dense rental stock. Employment leans heavily on agriculture and the nearby Chico economy — Enloe Medical Center, Chico State, and almond-processing operations are major employers within commuting range — so this is functionally a bedroom community with a short, uncongested drive north on Highway 99. Summers are blazing (average highs well into the 90s from June through September) and winters are mild and foggy, with the Sacramento Valley's famous tule fog settling in for days at a stretch. Durham's defining tension is that it offers Sacramento Valley affordability and genuine rural quiet just minutes from a university town's amenities, but virtually everything — groceries, restaurants, evening entertainment — requires a car trip out.
